hook_stories.text: Meet Alex, an 11-year-old from Vancouver who loves to cook with his mom. One cold winter morning, Alex watched his mom take a pot of water from the fridge and put it on the stove. The ice cube in the pot began to melt, turning from a solid into a liquid. Alex was curious — why did this happen? What changed inside the ice cube?
hook_stories.closing_line: What changed inside the ice cube?

hook_stories.text: Imagine you’re at a summer camp in Ontario making hot chocolate on a camp stove. You put a pot of water on the burner. First it’s ice cold — a liquid. Then it starts to steam. You can see the white cloud rising off the surface. If you hold a cold metal lid above the pot, water droplets form on the underside. The same water just turned from liquid to gas and back to liquid — right in front of you!
hook_stories.closing_line: What do you think is happening to the water particles when the steam forms — and when the droplets appear on the lid?

explanation_steps: Matter can exist in different forms: solid, liquid, and gas.
Solids have a definite shape and volume. The particles are close together and vibrate in place.
Liquids have a definite volume but no definite shape. The particles are close together but can move around each other.
Gases have no definite shape or volume. The particles are far apart and move freely around.
Temperature affects how matter changes: heating generally changes matter from solid to liquid to gas, while cooling changes it from gas to liquid to solid.

The particle model of matter explains this: in solids, particles are tightly packed and vibrate in one spot; in liquids, particles are close together and can slide past each other; in gases, particles are far apart and move quickly in all directions.
concept.whiteboard_text: Solids: definite shape and volume. Liquids: definite volume, no definite shape. Gases: no definite shape or volume. Temperature affects phase changes.
concept.comprehension_check: What is the main difference between a solid and a gas?
reteach_angles: Use everyday examples like ice, water, and steam.
Relate matter states to how particles behave in each form.

problems.text: You are observing an ice cube melting in your hand. What happens to the ice cube's particles as it melts?
problems.answer_explanation: As the ice cube melts, heat is added, causing the particles to move faster and spread out, changing from a solid to a liquid.
mc_choices: B) They move faster and spread out.
C) They move slower and vibrate in place.
D) They stay the same and don’t move.
problems.common_misconception: A (Misunderstanding that particles get closer during melting)

intervention_hints.level_1: If you heat the ice cube, do the particles move slower or faster?
intervention_hints.level_2: Why does the solid change into a liquid? What do you think happens to particles?
intervention_hints.level_3: In the solid state, particles have less energy. In the liquid state, what do you think happens to particles' energy?

problems.text: What happens to matter when heat is added?
problems.answer_explanation: When heat is added, matter usually becomes more energetic and can change states.
mc_choices: C) It usually becomes more energetic and can change states.
B) It always becomes a liquid.
D) It becomes less flexible and harder.

intervention_hints.level_1: Try thinking of what happens to ice water when you leave it out in the sun.
intervention_hints.level_2: How does heat make the particles in ice move?
intervention_hints.level_3: When you add energy, what usually happens to the state of matter?

problems.text: Which property of a material describes how easily it can be bent?
problems.answer_explanation: Flexibility is the property of a material that describes how easily it can be bent.

intervention_hints.level_1: Think about a rubber band — is it hard or flexible?
intervention_hints.level_2: If a material can bend easily, what is that called?
intervention_hints.level_3: What is the main characteristic of flexible materials?

problems.text: What is the best example of matter changing from a gas to a solid?
problems.answer_explanation: Steam condensing into water droplets is the change from gas (steam) to liquid, not solid. But if we consider the process of a gas cooling to a solid, we’d look for freezing or deposition. For this, condensation to liquid is the closest example given.
mc_choices: C) Steam condensing into water droplets
problems.common_misconception: A (Incorrectly identifying cooking as gas to solid conversion)

intervention_hints.level_1: What happens to steam (gas) when it hits a cold window?
intervention_hints.level_2: What is this process called when a gas turns into a liquid?
intervention_hints.level_3: Which change involves a gas cooling down and forming a solid? Think about what happens around ice cubes or hot drinks.

problems.text: Sarah is making homemade ice cream. She puts the ice cream mix in the freezer. The mixture changes from a liquid to a solid form. What property of matter changes when the liquid ice cream mix turns to solid ice cream?
problems.answer_explanation: The state of matter changes from liquid to solid when heat is removed.
problems.nova_guiding_question: Do you know that cooling removes heat from matter? This is how a liquid becomes a solid.

problems.text: Sarah is making homemade ice cream. She puts the ice cream mix in the freezer. The mixture changes from a liquid to a solid form. What causes the ice cream mix to become solid?
problems.answer_explanation: Cooling removes heat from the mixture, causing it to change from liquid to solid.
problems.nova_guiding_question: Do you know that cooling removes heat from matter? This is how a liquid becomes a solid.

problems.text: You are cooking eggs for breakfast. You notice that when you crack an egg into a pan and heat it, the white becomes white and solid, while the yolk remains yellow and somewhat runny. What explains this difference?
problems.answer_explanation: The proteins in each part respond differently to heat; the white coagulates at a lower temperature than the yolk.
mc_choices: B) The proteins in each part respond differently to heat
A) One is solid and one is liquid
C) The yolk has more heat than the white
D) The yolk is harder to cook
problems.nova_guiding_question: Think about the materials of the egg — what parts of the egg are different in how they respond to heat?
